(a) MONOTONE HALF, free: deleting a capability can only make an instance MORE infeasible, so an INFEASIBLE reading cannot have been caused by a spurious capability -- certified with no solve. (b) FEASIBLE readings: re-solve with each capability deleted; certify iff feasible under every single deletion.
predict: soundness 1.000 among certified (the theorem gives it, conditional on the rest of the reading). Coverage: all infeasible answers free (~35%), plus 30-60% of the feasible ones, so 55-75% overall. The 42 false-FEASIBLE cases should be refused almost entirely, because each is feasible ONLY through the spurious capability -- deleting it flips them.
would_refute: certified-and-wrong cases, which would mean a second channel is live (the job-side distractor is off in this arm, so there should not be one); or near-zero coverage on the feasible side, which would make the check sound and useless and would mean scheduling's NP-hard decision denies insensitivity the way solvency's sum does.
cost_note: k+1 solves where k is the number of has_capability claims, about 6 -- against 1.2ms/case at the default regime. Must be priced, not just scored.

verdict: soundness exactly as the theorem predicts; coverage on the feasible side over-called by 3x; and it CORRECTS my own morning headline
measured: 200 cases, default regime. clean: acc 1.000, coverage 0.665, acc|cert 1.000, cover|feasible 0.056, 1.80 solves. HARD MACHINE: acc 0.790 with 42 false-FEASIBLE, coverage 0.525, acc|cert 1.000, 0 WRONG, cover|feasible 0.159, 3.07 solves, 3.42 ms/case.
the_correction: this morning I concluded a multi-valued channel leaves only fixing the reader, because every DETECTOR fires 0.000 on it. Too strong: insensitivity needs no second source and no arity. All 42 unsound answers are refused, because each is feasible ONLY through the spurious capability. 21% silent unsound error becomes 47.5% refusal at 1.000 soundness.
free_half: 43.5% of coverage costs nothing -- deleting a has_capability can only make an instance MORE infeasible, so an infeasible reading is certified with no extra solve. The monotone half again, the one already known to transfer to scheduling.
over_called: predicted 30-60% coverage among feasible readings; measured 0.056 clean and 0.159 hard. At slack 0.15 almost every capability is load-bearing, so the certificate is nearly 'infeasible => certified' plus a sliver.
third_instance_but_with_a_distinction: cover|feasible RISES 0.056 -> 0.159 on the corrupt surface because the spurious capability ADDS REDUNDANCY. Unlike the flood and solvency cases it does NOT cost soundness here, because the corruption lies inside the hypothesis the check enumerates. APPARENT STABILITY CREATED BY A CHANNEL THE CERTIFICATE COVERS IS REAL; CREATED BY ONE IT DOES NOT, IT IS AN ILLUSION.
price: solves 1.00 -> 3.07, correct answers 158 -> 105, PRICE OF SOUNDNESS 4.62x (flood was 13.4x before its certificate, 1.0x after). And usd_per_solved_above_floor makes this row WORSE however sound it is -- the gap cost.py's own docstring names.

gap: cost.py's north star, usd_per_solved_above_floor, COUNTS ANSWERS -- so a certificate that refuses half of them makes the row worse however sound it is. Its own docstring names the gap: 'prices getting the answer right and prices knowing you are right at zero'. Today produced THREE certificates whose entire value is soundness and the metric cannot see any of them.
the_fix: express the caller's decision as a NUMBER instead of a hedge. Answering: utility per case a - W(1-a) at compute c0. Certifying: utility k (soundness 1.000) at compute c1. Certifying wins iff W > [a - k*c0/c1] / (1-a). That break-even W -- what a wrong answer must cost relative to a right one -- is computable per domain from numbers already measured.
predict: scheduling ~3 (a=0.790, k=0.525, c1/c0=3.07 gives (0.790-0.171)/0.210 = 2.95). Flood's link certificate and solvency's membership certificate should come out at or below ZERO -- both are ~1x compute and their certified set is a subset of what the collapsing reader already got right, so they strictly dominate and are free lunches at any wrong-answer cost. An informative spread: two certificates that are unconditionally worth taking and one that is a real trade.
would_refute: a scheduling break-even below 1, which would mean the certificate pays even when a wrong answer costs no more than a right one -- i.e. I have mis-stated the compute multiple.

verdict: right on two of three, and the miss corrects a piece of my own reasoning
measured: break-even W -- what one wrong answer must cost in units of one right one -- for the three certificates on their honest surfaces: solvency membership FREE (acc 0.485, coverage 0.485, 1.00x compute); flood role-independent 0.60x (0.679, 0.488, 1.00x); scheduling capability 2.95x (0.790, 0.525, 3.07x). Predicted scheduling 2.95 exactly.
the_miss: predicted flood and solvency would BOTH be free, on the grounds that each certificate's certified set is a SUBSET of what the collapsing reader already got right. True and NOT SUFFICIENT: free requires coverage/m >= rate, i.e. the certificate must keep MOST of the correct answers. Flood keeps 0.488 of 0.679 -- 72% -- so 28% of its correct answers are given up and something must pay for them. Solvency is free because its coverage EQUALS its accuracy: certified <=> correct on that arm.
shipped: symbolic_ai_core.cost.break_even_wrong_cost. Prices soundness against ACCURACY, not against the floor, so it is a companion to usd_per_solved_above_floor and not a replacement -- a system below its floor has bought nothing whatever a wrong answer costs. Treats a refusal as worth zero; a pipeline that escalates a refusal is cost.Targeting's job.

question: The signature-determinacy audit is this repo's most load-bearing instrument -- credited with predicting reader difficulty, where error concentrates, payback and maintenance. It has only ever been computed on surfaces built to make signatures computable. How much INFORMATION does a sentence signature carry on English nobody here wrote?
method: H(signature) in bits over a sentence population, plus the top-bucket share, on (a) the three synthetic surfaces and (b) 36k scientific abstracts and 75k narrative sentences. A signature reader can distinguish at most 2^H predicates, so this bounds the whole approach on real text with the repo's own tool. Entity detection on real text is CRUDE -- capitalised spans not sentence-initial, plus acronyms -- and it OVER-counts, which INFLATES real-text entropy, so a low number is conservative.
predict: synthetic surfaces 3-4 bits with a small top bucket (each claim kind gets its own signature; that is what 0.000 ambiguity mass means). Real prose 1.5-2.5 bits with a top bucket of 40-60%, because most sentences carry 0-1 entities, no number and no date. Conclusion expected: on real text the signature has at most ~4 distinguishable classes, against domains with 9-12 claim kinds, so signature-determinacy is a property of the BENCHMARK rather than a general reading discipline.
would_refute: real-text entropy at or above the synthetic surfaces -- which would mean real sentences are MORE signature-distinguishable than the generated ones, and the whole instrument transfers.

verdict: REFUTED as predicted-in-advance, and pursuing why produced the better instrument
measured: entropy of the sentence signature: flood 2.59 bits, scheduling 2.26, solvency 2.61 (generated) against abstracts 3.65 and narrative 2.06. I predicted synthetic 3-4 and real 1.5-2.5; real abstracts carry MORE signature entropy than any generated surface, which was my stated refutation condition.
why_the_statistic_was_wrong: ENTROPY SAYS HOW MUCH A SIGNATURE VARIES, NOT HOW MUCH IT DETERMINES. Determinacy is a property of the JOINT distribution of signature and predicate; a population can have arbitrarily high signature entropy and zero determinacy. I reached for entropy because it needs no labels, which is exactly why it cannot answer the question labels are for -- and 'it was computable' is the wrong reason to choose a statistic.
what_survives_and_is_exact: kinds per bucket. On the generated surfaces the spans carry the kind: flood top bucket 0.455 holding 2 kinds -> mass 0.860 (the known raw figure, reproduced as a check); scheduling 0.291 holding 1 -> 0.000; solvency 0.509 holding 1 -> 0.000. A BUCKET CAN BE HUGE AND HOLD ONE KIND -- that is what a determinate surface looks like.
the_real_text_bound: the largest signature in BOTH real corpora is the EMPTY one -- no entity, no number, no date -- holding 15,996 of 36,223 abstract sentences (44.2%) and 35,413 of 75,555 narrative ones (46.9%), and the samples are plainly different predicates (contributed_to, was_realised, includes, is_not). So ambiguity mass on real prose is AT LEAST 0.44 against the 0.000 scheduling and solvency post -- and 0.000 is the reading the repo uses to argue a content-free reader can work.
structural_and_detector_independent: a signature over (entity counts, numbers, dates) NEVER LOOKS AT THE VERB, and the verb is where a real predicate lives. A better NER moves sentences between buckets; it does not make 'contributed to', 'is realized' and 'include' distinguishable by shape.

target: the declared floor: 'sub_98 left the group in April' is semantically stale, has the ownership signature exactly, and carries NO declared cancellation cue. Every lexical check built today is silent on it. The signature-bits result says why -- a signature over (entity counts, numbers, dates) NEVER LOOKS AT THE VERB, and the verb is where the predicate lives.
resource: WordNet is on disk at ~/nltk_data/corpora/wordnet.zip and readable without any new dependency: index.verb gives 11,529 lemmas, data.verb gives each synset's lex_filenum, and lexnames maps 29-43 to the fifteen verb supersenses. Using a real standard rather than re-deriving one.
hypothesis: a relation claim is STATIVE (own, hold, sit inside, be set up for, is joined by) and a stale sentence asserts a TRANSITION (leave, divest, withdraw, resign, cease). WordNet supersenses should separate them: verb.motion / verb.social / verb.change against verb.stative.
predict: PARTIAL separation. Motion and social verbs (leave, resign, withdraw, depart) should not overlap the stative relation verbs, so those get caught. verb.possession will OVERLAP BADLY -- `own` and `hold` are possession verbs just as `divest` and `sell` are -- so possession-verb staleness is expected to be missed, and a rule keying on possession would fire on the real claims. Expect to catch roughly half of a held-out stale set at zero false positives on the real claims, or to find that no rule separates them at all.
protocol_against_my_own_trap: I will look at the domains' verbs to design the rule, which is the constructed-to-pass risk I wrote a lesson about this morning. So the rule is evaluated on a HELD-OUT set built afterwards from WordNet verbs in the chosen classes that were not consulted while designing it.
a_null_is_publishable_here: if no supersense rule separates transition from state, that is the finding: the floor is real and lexical semantics does not lift it.

verdict: partial separation as predicted, and the held-out protocol earned its keep -- the design set inflated recall twofold
measured: (1) SUPERSENSES CANNOT SEPARATE transition from state: cease=verb.stative, divest=verb.possession, exactly like own; the union is worse, `left` carries stative among six classes. (2) HYPERNYM CLOSURE can: all-8 roots design recall 0.86 / HELD-OUT 0.42 / FP 0.08; deep-6 roots 0.64 / HELD-OUT 0.33 / FP 0.00. (3) At the SENTENCE level on 10,650 real abstract sentences: all-8 fires 0.522, deep-6 0.058, against 0.003 for the cancellation gate.
the_reusable_lesson: AN ANCESTOR'S USEFULNESS IS SET BY ITS DEPTH, AND DEPTH MUST BE MEASURED AGAINST A LARGE NEGATIVE POPULATION, NOT A HAND-LISTED ONE. Token fires per root: change 6,899, transfer 2,191, then a cliff -- leave 315, end 271, remove 91, exit 12, deprive 5. Two shallow ancestors are 95% of the firing, and I chose them against a FIFTEEN-verb negative class.
corrects_my_own_framing: a nominal filter moves 0.522 -> 0.426 and 0.058 -> 0.045, so PART OF SPEECH IS NOT THE DOMINANT PROBLEM -- ancestor depth is. An hour earlier I named POS tagging as the missing capability.
end_to_end: solvency with the consolidated reader: the verb gate LIFTS the uncued floor 0.485 -> 0.635 (first thing all day that moves it by READING) and DESTROYS the clean surface 1.000 -> 0.650 on ONE WORD -- `dated`, a participial modifier in every filing sentence whose first WordNet sense is the romantic one and whose chain reaches `leave`. Both failure modes in a single token.
the_fallback_was_predicted_to_fail: flag-rather-than-delete plus emission cannot work here, and this afternoon's decision note says why BEFORE the experiment: solvency's decision is a SUM, every filing moves it, and an aggregating decision admits neither response. Kept and MARKED rather than shipped -- stale_by_verb carries the numbers, because a dead end nobody writes down gets re-derived.

verdict: the floor IS liftable, in one domain, and the same gate destroys another -- which is the real finding
measured: SENSE DOMINANCE not sense priority: requiring the transition reading on >20% of a lemma's senses removes `dated` (0.20) while every genuine transition verb sits at 0.27+ and every relation verb at 0.00. With it, solvency uncued owns goes 0.475 -> 1.000 AT NO COST ON THE CLEAN SURFACE -- the first thing all day that moves that arm by READING. Threshold set by one false positive and labelled fitted; it costs nothing, since held-out recall is 0.33 both with it and with the first-sense rule it replaces.
and_then: flood 0.589 -> 0.014, scheduling 0.767 -> 0.675. `can` is what kills flood -- WordNet has it as a verb ('terminate the employment of'), one of two senses reaches `remove`, fraction 0.5, and it appears 90 times in thirty documents. SENSE DOMINANCE PROTECTS AGAINST A RARE WRONG SENSE AND NOT AGAINST A LOW-SENSE-COUNT WORD: `dated` is 1 of 5 and caught, `can` is 1 of 2 and not.
the_contrast_is_the_finding: stale_by_cancellation is CLOSED-CLASS (11 cues), fires on 0.004 of real prose, and leaves all three generated surfaces BYTE-IDENTICAL. stale_by_verb is OPEN-CLASS (11,529 lemmas), fires on 0.156, and moves the three by +0.525 / -0.092 / -0.575. A CLOSED-CLASS FEATURE TRANSFERS; AN OPEN-CLASS LEXICON DOES NOT -- its false-positive rate grows with the vocabulary and a deletion gate's damage grows with the surface's CLAIM DENSITY, and the two multiply.
also: the remaining solvency arm stays 0.492 because its distractor is not stale at all -- an unofficial figure was never true rather than withdrawn, which is the insensitivity response's job.
tooling: uv add nltk followed by uv remove nltk SILENTLY DROPPED THE `solvers` EXTRA, taking z3-solver and clingo out of the environment. pyproject.toml was never modified so nothing was committed wrong; uv sync --extra solvers restored it. A plain uv run re-syncs to default extras.

why: every number in this repo is measured on text it generated itself, and every structured source on disk was normalised into node/edge tables with the prose stripped -- checked on cfpb, senate-lda, sec-edgar, patentsview, cskg, gutenberg. Wikidata P749 (parent organization) plus the Wikipedia intro is PAIRED prose and fact, it is the real-world analogue of solvency's `owns`, and it carries the day's hardest problem natively: company articles are full of FORMER parents.
predict: (a) a naive pattern extractor finds an ownership mention in 50-70% of intros and names the gold parent in 40-60% of those. (b) The cancellation gate SHOULD help, since 'formerly a subsidiary of X' is exactly what it is built for.
the_primary_hypothesis_and_it_is_the_one: THE GATE WILL HURT, NOT HELP, AND FOR A REASON THAT INDICTS THE WHOLE DESIGN. On generated surfaces one sentence carries ONE claim, so deleting a stale sentence is safe. Real prose packs several claims into a sentence -- 'Formerly a subsidiary of X, it was acquired by Y in 2015' carries both the dead parent and the live one -- so a SENTENCE-LEVEL gate cannot be right. If that shows up it is the first test of the GRANULARITY of this repo's claim model against real text, and it says the unit of staleness is a CLAUSE, not a sentence.
would_refute_that: the gate improving precision with no recall loss, which would mean real prose separates its claims by sentence after all and the generated surfaces are not misleading about granularity.

verdict: PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED -- the sentence gate hurts, and for the reason predicted
measured: 148 companies, Wikidata P749 + Wikipedia intro. CEILING: the current parent is named in the intro on only 0.696 of articles. Wikidata lists a FORMER parent for 0.149 and the intro names one on 0.115. stale_by_cancellation flags a sentence on 0.338 of these articles, against 0.004 of scientific abstracts -- company prose is DENSE in cancellation language. Arms: naive answers 0.622 / correct 0.392 / precision 0.630 / picks-former 0.027; SENTENCE GATE 0.568 / 0.351 / 0.619 / 0.027; CLAUSE GATE 0.615 / 0.378 / 0.615 / 0.020.
the_finding: THE SENTENCE GATE LOSES COVERAGE AND ACCURACY AND REMOVES NO STALENESS AT ALL -- eight answers and 0.041 accuracy gone, former-parent error unmoved. The clause gate keeps coverage and is the only arm that reduces the error the gates exist for. Worked example MIRAMAX (current beIN/Paramount, former Filmyard/Walt Disney): sentence gate answers 'Walt Disney Company', a FORMER parent, because it kept the sentence naming the dead owner and deleted the one naming the live one. Three more go from an answer to NO ANSWER under the sentence gate.
what_it_says_about_everything_built_toda: on the generated surfaces ONE SENTENCE CARRIES ONE CLAIM, so deleting a flagged sentence is free and stale_by_cancellation left all three byte-identical. Real prose packs several claims into a sentence. THE UNIT OF STALENESS IS A CLAUSE, NOT A SENTENCE, AND THE GENERATED SURFACES COULD NOT HAVE SHOWN THAT. A defect in the BENCHMARK'S GRANULARITY, not in the gate -- the audit's spans, unconsumed, evidence_conflict and filter_stale all assume one claim per sentence and none of that has been tested against text nobody here wrote.
the_sobering_proportion: the former-parent error is 2.7% of articles; precision among answered is 0.63 against a ceiling of 0.696. On real text the staleness problem that took a day is a SMALL SLICE of the error, and the dominant one is that extraction is hard. Perfect staleness handling moves accuracy 0.392 -> 0.419.

why: the Wikipedia arm measured the one-claim-per-sentence assumption FALSE on real prose, and that assumption is baked into the audit's spans, unconsumed, evidence_conflict and filter_stale. The constructive response is to fix the BENCHMARK: give each generator a `packed` option that renders two claims in one sentence, then see which mechanisms survive.
predict: (a) SOLVENCY breaks hardest. 'group owns sub_0, which reported 105.87 USD on 29 May 2026' has 2 entities AND money AND a date, and read_signature's branches are exclusive -- 2-entity requires no money and no dates -- so NO branch matches and BOTH claims are lost. Expect accuracy to collapse toward the majority floor. (b) SCHEDULING breaks: 'machine_0 is set up for cut and has 5.51 hours available' hits the capacity branch first and the capability branch is an elif, so the CAPABILITY is silently dropped -- the unsound direction again. (c) FLOOD LARGELY SURVIVES, and for a reason worth checking: read_content_roles already merges crossings into links, so packing link+load_limit into one sentence is harmless there.
the_hypothesis_i_care_about: THE AUDIT SHOULD PREDICT THE DAMAGE. Packing raises the ambiguity mass of the packed surface offline, before any reader runs, and the ranking of the three domains' accuracy drop should follow the ranking of their mass increase. The audit has had a run of things it CANNOT predict (which channels are erroneous, vocabulary fragility, real-prose determinacy); this is the case where it should come out ahead, and if it does not that is worse news for the instrument than any of them.
would_refute: a domain whose mass is unchanged by packing but whose reader still collapses -- which would mean the damage is in the reader's branch ORDER rather than in the signature, and the audit is blind to control flow.

verdict: every part of the prediction held, and the audit finally came out ahead
measured: solvency ambiguity mass 0.000 -> 0.741 with accuracy 1.000 -> 0.567 (its floor exactly); scheduling mass 0.000 -> 0.279 with accuracy 1.000 -> 0.658 (its floor exactly). BOTH READERS COLLAPSE TO THEIR FLOOR -- solvency returns one constant verdict on every case and scheduling loses half the floor's capabilities.
the_mechanism_in_one_diff: scheduling seed 0, has_capability unpacked [(m0,cut),(m0,weld),(m1,cut),(m1,paint)] vs packed [(m0,weld),(m1,paint)]. Capacities all survive. read_signature branches on shape with an ELIF chain, so a packed sentence matches the capacity branch and the capability branch never runs.
the_audit_predicts_it_offline: mass rises before any reader runs and ranks solvency as the worse case. FIRST THING TODAY THE INSTRUMENT GETS AHEAD OF -- it could not predict which channels are erroneous, nor vocabulary fragility, nor real-prose determinacy.
and_it_is_a_theorem_not_a_measurement: a signature is a FUNCTION OF THE SENTENCE, so a sentence realising two kinds is ambiguous BY DEFINITION and ambiguity_mass is bounded below by the share of multi-claim sentences. NO SIGNATURE READER CAN BE PACKING-ROBUST, and real prose is packed. That closes the loop from the Wikipedia finding: the sentence is the wrong unit AND the signature is defined on it.
the_actionable_rule: ACCUMULATE, DO NOT BRANCH. Flood survives packing because read_content_roles writes crossings into a dict and folds them into links rather than selecting a branch -- it is not signature-based at that point. A reader assigning into per-kind stores can take several claims from one sentence; one selecting a branch per sentence cannot, and no signature refinement changes that. It is a property of CONTROL FLOW, which is what the audit is blind to.

claim_under_test: the packing finding produced one actionable rule -- ACCUMULATE, DO NOT BRANCH -- derived from flood being the only reader that survives a packed sentence. A rule derived from one accidental case is a hypothesis, not a design principle. This builds it deliberately for the two readers that collapsed.
design: for each sentence, extract EVERY claim pattern independently instead of selecting one branch by shape. Solvency: >=2 entities enrols members; an (entity, money, date) co-occurrence files a figure, attached to the entity NEAREST the money -- positional adjacency, content-free, the same signal flood uses for its demand. Scheduling: a machine sentence yields its capacity AND any capability words in it, not one or the other.
predict: both recover to 1.000 on the packed surface and stay 1.000 unpacked, because nothing else about the packing is hard -- the claims are all there, the reader was simply discarding them. If that holds, the rule is validated and the repo gains two packing-robust readers.
would_refute: the nearest-entity heuristic mis-assigning filings in packed sentences ('group owns sub_0, which reported 105.87 USD' -- the filer is sub_0, the entity NEAREST the number, not the subject), which would show that accumulation needs a binding rule as well as a scan and that flood's survival was easier than it looks.
note: unpacked accuracy must not move. Any drop there means the accumulating reader is admitting claims the branching one correctly refused, which is the precision failure this repo keeps finding.

verdict: confirmed on all four cells, and the refutation condition did not fire
measured: solvency branch 1.000 unpacked / 0.567 packed; consolidated the same; ACCUMULATE 1.000 / 1.000. scheduling branch 1.000 / 0.658; ACCUMULATE 1.000 / 1.000. And on every HONEST surface the accumulating readers are IDENTICAL to the branching ones -- solvency 1.000 / 0.475 / 0.475 / 0.433 across clean, owns-cued, owns-uncued, both-uncued; scheduling 1.000 / 0.767 / 0.967 across clean, hard-machine, hard-job. STRICT DOMINATION.
the_refutation_that_did_not_fire: I flagged that the nearest-entity binding might mis-assign filings in packed sentences. It does not: 'group owns sub_0, which reported 105.87 USD' binds to sub_0, the entity beside the number rather than the subject. Positional adjacency, content-free, the same signal flood uses for its demand. Pinned by a test.
what_it_settles: the rule was derived from flood surviving BY ACCIDENT, which is a hypothesis rather than a principle. Built deliberately in the two domains where it did not hold, it recovers everything packing took at zero cost, so ACCUMULATE-DO-NOT-BRANCH is a design principle.
and_it_sharpens_the_theorem: packing_ambiguity says no reader can decide a packed sentence's kind FROM ITS SIGNATURE, because a signature is a function of the sentence. It does NOT say the claims are unrecoverable -- they are all there. What the signature loses is the CLASSIFICATION; what accumulation recovers is the CONTENT.

goal: turn the Wikipedia observation into a REPEATABLE BENCHMARK CASE. Miramax failed because one sentence carried a dead owner and a live one and the sentence gate deleted the wrong half. No generated surface can produce that, so the finding is currently unreproducible here.
build: a `stale_clause` option for solvency that prefixes a REAL member's filing sentence with a former-parent clause: 'sub_0, formerly a subsidiary of holdco, reported 105.87 USD, filed 29 May 2026.' The stale clause is irrelevant; the filing is needed. That is Miramax in miniature.
predict: branch reader with NO gate: 2 entities AND money AND a date matches no branch, so the filing is lost -> wrong. ACCUMULATING reader with no gate: correct, because it enrols both entities (holdco harmlessly, since it files nothing) and binds the filing to the entity nearest the money. SENTENCE GATE: deletes the whole sentence, loses sub_0's filing, breaks the accumulating reader. CLAUSE GATE: keeps the filing clause, restores it.
the_headline_if_it_holds: a sentence-level staleness gate is not merely useless on packed prose but ACTIVELY HARMFUL -- it takes a reader that was right and makes it wrong -- and the benchmark can now show that without leaving the repo.
would_refute: the accumulating reader failing without any gate, which would mean packing plus staleness is a harder problem than packing alone and accumulation is not sufficient.

verdict: the headline held and the refutation condition HALF-FIRED, which sharpened it
measured: 120 seeds, six cells. branch: clean 1.000, stale_clause 0.625 with no gate, 0.625 with the sentence gate, 1.000 with the clause gate. accumulate: 1.000 clean, 0.925 no gate, 0.625 SENTENCE GATE, 1.000 clause gate.
the_headline: THE SENTENCE GATE TAKES 0.925 TO 0.625 -- it does not merely fail to help, it takes a reader that was mostly right and makes it wrong. The Miramax mechanism, now reproducible without leaving the repo.
the_half_refutation: I predicted accumulation would be correct with no gate; it is 0.925. The nearest-money binding is WRONG FOR THIS SHAPE -- the parenthetical sits closer to the number than the subject does, so some filings bind to sub_97. Right for 'group owns sub_0, which reported...', wrong for 'sub_0, formerly..., reported...', and the two shapes are equally natural. It shows as 0.925 rather than 0.5 only because the verdict is a threshold test and one lost filing rarely crosses it.
the_elegant_part: the clause gate does TWO jobs at once. It removes the dead claim AND the second entity that made the binding ambiguous -- after filtering the sentence is 'sub_0 reported 105.87 USD, filed 29 May 2026', one entity, nothing to guess. A GATE THAT CUTS AT THE RIGHT GRANULARITY DOES NOT JUST DELETE LESS, IT SIMPLIFIES WHAT IS LEFT.
shipped: filter_stale(..., unit='clause'), with 'sentence' kept as the default so earlier numbers keep their meaning. The Wikipedia script now calls the shipped function -- one implementation -- and reproduces the ordering on real text: naive 0.589/0.369, sentence 0.548/0.339, clause 0.583/0.357 with the former-parent error 0.024 -> 0.018.
surface_trap_pinned: the stale clause must name a REAL entity id. With an unmatched word the reader sees one entity, nothing is packed, and the case is quietly easy -- a test asserts sub_97 is in the rendered line.

question: 'clause, not sentence' answers WHICH of two units, not whether there is an optimum. If the right rule were simply 'cut as small as possible', the clause result would be a way-station and the finest split would win. Sweep the granularity -- document, sentence, clause, fine (coordinators and relative pronouns), finest (also prepositional heads) -- on both the Wikipedia corpus and the generated stale_clause surface.
predict: U-SHAPED, with the optimum at clause. Splitting finer breaks the patterns themselves: 'a subsidiary of X' spans an of-boundary, so a splitter that cuts there destroys the very mention the reader is looking for, and accuracy falls below the naive arm. If that holds, THE UNIT IS A REAL LINGUISTIC OBJECT rather than 'as small as you can manage', and the fix has a principled stopping point instead of a slider.
would_refute: monotone improvement down to the finest split, which would mean the gate's whole problem is over-deletion and the right advice is simply to cut as fine as the tokeniser allows.

verdict: U-SHAPE CONFIRMED on both corpora, and the mechanism came out cleaner than predicted
measured: WIKIPEDIA (168 intros) answers/accuracy/picks-former: document 0.589/0.369/0.024; sentence 0.542/0.327/0.024; clause 0.583/0.357/0.018; FINE 0.589/0.375/0.018; finest 0.542/0.327/0.024. SOLVENCY stale_clause, accumulating reader, 120 seeds: document 0.925, sentence 0.592, clause 1.000, fine 1.000, finest 0.925.
the_identity_that_makes_it_a_finding: THE FINEST SPLIT REPRODUCES THE SENTENCE SPLIT'S NUMBERS TO THREE DECIMALS IN EVERY COLUMN. A splitter fine enough to cut THROUGH the pattern being looked for ('a subsidiary OF X') leaves no fragment matching it, which is indistinguishable from deleting the sentence. OVER-SPLITTING IS OVER-DELETING BY ANOTHER ROUTE. So the unit is a real linguistic object rather than a slider, and the fix has a principled stopping point: cut at boundaries the patterns do not cross.
what_n_168_does_not_resolve: which of clause and fine is best -- 0.018 apart, three articles, and tied at 1.000 on the generated case. `fine` is the ONLY arm that beats no filtering at all (0.375 vs 0.369) while halving the former-parent error, and that margin is ONE ARTICLE. NOT shipping a third option on one article; filter_stale keeps sentence (default) and clause, and the sweep is recorded so a later session does not rediscover that finer is not better.

question: Inspectability is one of the five properties APPROACH.md argues for, and it has only ever been checked on the EASY surface. `ungrounded` already carries a scope note saying it certifies consistency with the world AS READ, not truth -- so on the honest surface, where the reader admits phantom links, an explanation can cite a claim that is FALSE and pass every check the repo has.
measure: flood, hard_distractors interleaved. Render the answer from the READ world, then check every claim: citation against the TRUE world. Report the share of explanations citing at least one false fact, split by whether the ANSWER was right.
predict: 20-40% of explanations cite a false claim overall. The number I actually care about is the split: I expect it to be NON-ZERO AMONG CORRECT ANSWERS, because the route is computed over the read graph and a phantom link can lie on a route whose bottleneck is set elsewhere. A CORRECT ANSWER WITH A FABRICATED JUSTIFICATION is exactly the failure mode a symbolic pipeline is supposed to be immune to, and if it happens here the inspectability claim needs the same qualifier the soundness claims got today.
would_refute: zero false citations among correct answers, which would mean the renderer only ever cites claims the answer actually depends on and those are exactly the ones the reader got right -- a real property, and one worth knowing.

verdict: predicted non-zero fabrication on correct answers; measured 0.076, and the mechanism is sharper than the prediction
measured: 300 seeds, flood interleaved, answers rendered from the READ world with every claim citation checked against the TRUE one. template/clean acc 0.985, 2.01 cites, 0.0025 false-per-cite, 0.005 any-false, 0.000 when CORRECT; template/honest identical per-citation (0.0025) with 0.000 when correct; complete/clean 11.74 cites, 0.0117, 0.066, 0.052 when correct; COMPLETE/HONEST 11.56 cites, 0.0388 false-per-cite, 0.378 any-false, 0.076 WHEN CORRECT. ungrounded flags 0.000 in EVERY cell.
1_a_correct_answer_with_a_fabricated_jus: 7.6% of the answers the complete renderer got RIGHT cite at least one false fact. That is the failure mode a symbolic pipeline is supposed to be immune to.
2_not_a_volume_effect: per citation the complete renderer is 15.5x worse on the honest surface (0.0388 vs 0.0025), because the extra facts it cites are the LOAD-BEARING SET COMPUTED FROM THE READ WORLD -- exactly where a phantom link lives. Citing more is not the problem; citing what the answer DEPENDS ON is, when the answer depends on something invented.
3_the_template_renderer_is_surface_indep: 0.0025 per citation on both surfaces and 0.000 fabrication on correct answers in both. It cites the demand and the site, which the reader gets right whatever the distractors do.
what_it_does_to_the_earlier_finding: 'an explanation that omits nothing material, for 37% MORE WORDS' priced completeness in LENGTH. Wrong currency. The price is TRUTH: 0.005 -> 0.378 explanations containing a falsehood and 0.000 -> 0.076 on correct answers.
defect_found_in_passing: the citation scheme is NOT UNIFORM -- some sources are a claim index (claim:7) and some a predicate name (claim:needs, claim:flooded). A citation that cannot be resolved to a claim cannot be checked against anything. Recorded, not fixed: fixing it would move every citation offset in the published numbers.

the_measurement_that_prompted_it: false citations by predicate on the honest surface, 300 seeds: mass 0/528, capacity 0/528, needs 0/392, demand 0/196, bridge_on 0/18, load_limit 0/18 -- SIX PREDICATES PERFECTLY HONEST over 1,680 citations. flooded 13/295 (0.044), depot 13/196 (0.066), and LINK 61/95 (0.642). 87 false of 2,266, and 70% of them are one predicate.
why_that_is_not_a_coincidence: it is the day's arity law, read off the citations. `link` is MULTI-VALUED with no corroborating source -- detection fires 0.000 on it -- so two thirds of cited links are phantom. depot/flooded are the ROLE channel, which the role flag does detect. Everything registry- or adjacency-corroborated is at ZERO.
build: the complete renderer cannot be made honest -- nothing in this repo checks a link. But it can be made to SAY WHERE IT IS NOT. Mark a citation as UNCORROBORATED iff its predicate lacks a second source: `link` always, and depot/flooded when role_assignment_forced is False.
predict: coverage of the false citations near 1.000, since all 87 are link, depot or flooded, in roughly 10-15% of the citations. If that holds, an explanation can flag its own risk exactly where the risk is, and inspectability stops being 'here are eleven facts' and becomes 'here are eleven facts, four of which nothing corroborates'.
would_refute: false citations outside those three predicates, which would mean corroboration is not what separates the honest ones and the partition is a coincidence of this surface.

verdict: prediction confirmed and tighter than expected -- recall 1.000 in 7.5% of citations
measured: false citations by predicate over 300 seeds and 2,266 citations: mass 0/528, capacity 0/528, needs 0/392, demand 0/196, bridge_on 0/18, load_limit 0/18 -- SIX PREDICATES PERFECTLY HONEST over 1,680 citations. flooded 13/295, depot 13/196, LINK 61/95 = 0.642. Links are 70% of the falsehoods and 4% of the citations.
the_marker: render.uncorroborated(answer, world, forced=...) flags citations resting on a claim nothing here can check -- `link` always, depot/flooded when role_assignment_forced is False. 88 false of 2,266; FLAGGED 171 (7.5%); FALSE CITATIONS FLAGGED 88/88 = 1.000. Every fabrication inside 7.5% of the text, a 13x concentration with no false negatives.
why_it_is_not_a_coincidence: it is the day's arity law read off the citations. link is multi-valued with no second source so detection fires 0.000 on it; depot/flooded are the role channel the flag does catch; everything corroborated by a value registry or by adjacency is at ZERO.
what_it_changes: the complete renderer CANNOT be made honest -- nothing checks a link and the arity law says nothing can. It can stop presenting eleven facts as one kind of thing: 'here are eleven facts, four of which nothing corroborates'. A third option beside the two-fact summary and the eleven-fact account, and the honest one.
limits: precision 0.51 -- half the flags are citations that happen to be right. And recall is 1.000 only because ALL 88 falsehoods are link/depot/flooded; a reader erring on a VALUE would fabricate inside a predicate this marks corroborated and the marker would miss it silently. The value registry is what stops that here, and it is a generator artefact.

testing_my_own_component: render.uncorroborated flagged 88 of 88 false citations. I stated the limit in the same breath: recall is 1.000 only because NO reader error here lands on a VALUE, and the thing that stops that is flood's VALUE_REGISTRY -- whose own docstring says the sets are 'the generator's own draw sets, unusually clean; a real registry would be noisier and would overlap'. So the marker's perfect recall may be an artefact of an idealisation the code already flags.
experiment: thread a `registry` parameter through read_content_roles and give it an OVERLAPPING one -- capacity values present in the mass set, as a real vocabulary would be. Then re-measure fabrication by predicate and the marker's recall.
predict: mass/capacity fabrications appear, and the marker MISSES them silently because it marks those predicates corroborated. Recall falls from 1.000 to somewhere in 0.5-0.8. End-to-end accuracy also falls, which is the first measurement of what the value registry is worth on the HONEST surface -- it has only ever been priced as a ceiling on the easy one.
would_refute: recall staying at 1.000, which would mean the mis-typed values never reach a citation -- possible, since the complete renderer cites the load-bearing set and a mis-slotted mass may simply make the answer empty rather than wrong-with-a-citation.

verdict: PREDICTION REFUTED, and the reason is the finding -- plus a number nobody had
measured: registry / accuracy / citations / false / flagged / marker recall: CLEAN 0.673 / 2266 / 88 / 0.075 / 1.000; OVERLAPPING 0.189 / 1452 / 27 / 0.061 / 1.000; NONE 0.000 / 280 / 27 / 0.361 / 1.000. False by predicate: clean link 61 flooded 14 depot 13; overlapping flooded 14 depot 13; none flooded 27.
the_refutation: I predicted the marker's recall would fall to 0.5-0.8 as value fabrications appeared. It stays 1.000 in all three and NO mass or capacity falsehood appears at any registry. A VALUE ERROR DOES NOT FABRICATE, IT SILENCES: a mis-slotted mass makes a vehicle fail to qualify, so no route is computed and nothing is cited about it. Citations fall 2266 -> 1452 -> 280 and the link fabrications vanish with them, 61 -> 0 -> 0 -- not because the reader improved but because it stopped answering. That was the refutation condition I wrote down BEFORE running.
number_nobody_had: THE VALUE REGISTRY IS WORTH THE ENTIRE CAPABILITY ON THE HONEST SURFACE, 0.673 -> 0.000. It had only ever been priced as a CEILING on the easy one. Every flood number here rests on a vocabulary of eleven numbers being exactly right.
methodological_catch: FABRICATION COUNTS FALL AS CAPABILITY FALLS -- 88 -> 27 -> 27 while accuracy goes 0.673 -> 0.189 -> 0.000. The most broken reader fabricates least in absolute terms because it says almost nothing. Per citation 0.039 -> 0.019 -> 0.096, not even monotone. REPORT FABRICATION AGAINST COVERAGE OR NOT AT ALL.
what_it_does_not_settle: the general limit. A domain whose values are routing INPUTS rather than qualification TESTS -- a cost to minimise, a capacity to divide -- would carry a mis-read value into the answer AND the citations, and the marker would miss it silently. The conditional to carry: values that GATE qualification silence; values that FEED the computation fabricate.

the_conditional_under_test: 'values that GATE qualification silence; values that FEED the computation fabricate.' Flood's values gate -- a mis-slotted mass disqualifies a vehicle and nothing is cited. Solvency's FEED: revenue figures are summed, and its renderer states the consolidated total as its central sentence.
experiment: render solvency's answer from the READ reading on the hard-FILING arm, where an unofficial figure is admitted and REPLACES the real one under latest-by-date. Compare the stated total against the truth, and check whether ungrounded fires.
predict: the explanation states a wrong consolidated total on nearly every case where the distractor is admitted -- the spurious figure is half the threshold, so the misstatement is large, on the order of tens of percent. ungrounded fires on none of it, same scope error as everywhere. That confirms the conditional at its worst: the fabricated number is not a peripheral citation but the HEADLINE of the explanation, and solvency's revenue channel is the one the day's law says admits NEITHER a second reading NOR insensitivity -- so nothing here can flag it.
would_refute: the stated total being right despite the wrong verdict, which would mean the renderer recomputes from something other than the read filings.

verdict: conditional confirmed, and the number is worse than predicted
measured: 200 seeds, rendered from the READ reading. clean: verdict wrong 0.000, stated total wrong 0.000, ungrounded 0.000. HARD FILING: verdict wrong 0.485, STATED TOTAL WRONG 1.000, mean relative error 0.398, ungrounded 0.000. hard both: 0.550 / 1.000 / 0.999 / 0.000.
the_finding: THE EXPLANATION IS WRONG TWICE AS OFTEN AS THE ANSWER. An admitted unofficial figure makes the stated consolidated total wrong on EVERY case while the verdict is wrong on 0.485, because a wrong sum only flips a threshold test when it crosses the threshold. MORE THAN HALF OF ALL CASES CARRY THE RIGHT VERDICT JUSTIFIED BY A FALSE NUMBER -- flood's version was 1 in 13, solvency's is 1 in 2, and the falsehood is the sentence the answer is ABOUT.
nothing_can_flag_it: ungrounded fires 0.000 and is right not to -- the spurious figure IS in the world as read. And render.uncorroborated cannot either: solvency's revenue channel is the one cell in the afternoon's table that admits NEITHER a second reading (multi-valued) NOR insensitivity (a sum). This is what that cell costs when someone reads the explanation.
the_general_statement: AN EXPLANATION'S ERROR RATE IS NOT BOUNDED BY THE ANSWER'S. A derived figure is wrong whenever ANY of its inputs is, while the answer is wrong only when the error crosses a decision boundary. So reporting accuracy says nothing about whether the account of it is true, and the gap GROWS with how much aggregation sits between the claims and the verdict. Inspectability is a free property of a symbolic pipeline only when the kernel uses claims DIRECTLY.
